scope: Nonprofits and faith-based civic organizations serving Macon-Bibb or Middle Georgia, explicitly referenced in the county outside-agency directory, 2026 grants and partnerships. A government reference is not an endorsement or proof of a county appointment. Named programs are identified as programs rather than separate legal entities. Corporate partners and public agencies are excluded from nonprofit classification. Leadership is added only where independently verified; no new portraits are taken from nonprofit websites. National educational resources directly linked by the county directory are also included. National educational resources directly linked by the county directory are also included.

existing.name: Community Foundation of Central Georgia
existing.description:
Macon-based community foundation founded in 1993 to encourage philanthropy and strengthen Central Georgia communities. CFCG serves 21 counties, including Bibb, through charitable funds, nonprofit grants, scholarships, and community partnerships. It works with individuals, families, businesses, and nonprofit organizations to support local needs and long-term charitable goals. Kathryn H. Dennis leads the staff as president; Cynde M. Dickey chairs the 2026-27 board.

Sources: https://cfcga.org/about/history-and-mission/ ; https://cfcga.org/about/counties/ ; https://cfcga.org/about/our-team/ ; https://cfcga.org/about/board-of-directors/

existing.name: NewTown Macon
existing.description:
Independent nonprofit working to revitalize downtown Macon by investing in local people and businesses. Its programs include business and real-estate financing, entrepreneur and developer training, downtown events, and the Ocmulgee Heritage Trail. Knight Foundation is a documented funder and partner. The current staff page lists James Fritze as president and CEO and Erin Keller as chief of staff and vice president for development.

Sources: https://newtownmacon.com/ ; https://newtownmacon.com/our-work/staff/ ; https://knightfoundation.org/articles/grantee-story/newtown-macon/

existing.name: Historic Macon Foundation
existing.description:
Macon preservation nonprofit working to strengthen neighborhoods by protecting historic architecture and sharing local history. Programs include neighborhood revitalization, historic-property rehabilitation, preservation consulting, educational programs, a tool library, and the Fading Five endangered-places initiative. The foundation formed in 2003 through the merger of the Middle Georgia Historical Society and Macon Heritage Foundation, with roots dating to 1964. Emily Hopkins is executive director.

Sources: https://historicmacon.org/who-we-are ; https://historicmacon.org/contact

organizations.name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation

existing.name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
existing.description:
National philanthropic foundation supporting journalism, arts, information and society, and community impact. Macon is one of its 26 communities with historic Knight newspaper ties. Its Macon investments support locally led revitalization and civic life; a Knight grantee story documents $1.5 million in support for NewTown Macon's work. The current staff directory lists Lynn Murphey as Director/Macon and Maribel Pérez Wadsworth as president and CEO.

Sources: https://knightfoundation.org/about/staff/ ; https://knightfoundation.org/articles/grantee-story/newtown-macon/

saved.name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation

existing.description:

Sources: https://unitedwaycg.org/our-staff ; https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/09/02/amid-downtown-business-concerns-macon-mulls-stricter-rules-for-the-homeless

existing.description:
Nonpartisan civic advocacy group founded in Middle Georgia in 2017, with documented organizing in Macon-Bibb County. existing.name: Bike Walk Macon
existing.description:
Grassroots bicycle and pedestrian advocacy nonprofit serving Macon-Bibb County. It promotes safer, more accessible walking, cycling, and transportation choices through advocacy, education, traffic-calming projects, and community events, including Open Streets Macon and Macon Bike Party. Its work began in 2015 with support from the Knight-funded Emerging City Champions fellowship. Kaylee Pruitt became executive director on May 20, 2026, succeeding founder Rachel Umana.
